items.title: US Department of Labor secures court order requiring New Jersey employer to pay $700K in back wages, damages to 48 workers denied overtime pay
items.content_text: VOORHEES, NJ – The U.S. Department of Labor has obtained a consent judgment and final order in federal district court requiring a New Jersey drywall installer to pay $725,000 in back wages, damages, and civil money penalties after denying 48 workers overtime pay.The department’s Wage and Hour Division found that P & B Partitions Inc. failed to pay their employees for pre-shift work while they waited for transportation to their jobsites. The failure to pay constitutes a violation under the Fair Labor Standards Act’s overtime provisions.  “Tasks completed to prepare for the job, and in this case, while waiting to get to the worksite, is work that must be compensated,” said Wage and Hour Division District Director Charlene Rachor in Southern New Jersey. “Failing to pay workers overtime wages deprives them of their rights, and we will hold employers accountable for such actions.”The consent judgment requires P & B Partitions Inc. to pay $350,000 in back wages, an equal amount in liquidated damages to 48 workers, and requires payment of an additional $25,000 in civil penalties. The judgment was entered in the U.S. District Court for the District of New Jersey on June 26, 2026.“The U.S. Department of Labor will pursue legal action to ensure that all employees receive the compensation they are legally owed,” said Regional Solicitor of Labor Jeffrey S. items.content_text: FMCSA announces its final decision to renew and modify the exemption granted to the Association of American Railroads and the American Short Line and Regional Railroad Association and member railroads (the Associations) from the hours-of-service (HOS) prohibitions against driving after the 14th hour after coming on duty (the 14-hour rule) and against driving after accumulating 60 hours of on duty time within 7 consecutive days, or 70 hours of on duty time within 8 consecutive days (the 60-hour/70-hour rule). The exemption will enable covered drivers to respond to unplanned events that occur outside of, or extend beyond, their normal work hours. FMCSA modifies the previous exemption to limit the categories of unplanned events during which the exemption may be used and to add reporting requirements. In addition, only drivers operating for motor carriers listed in the Appendix to this decision may operate under the exemption. FMCSA has analyzed the exemption application and has determined that the exemption renewal, subject to the terms and conditions set forth below, is likely to achieve a level of safety that is equivalent to or greater than the level that would be achieved in the absence of the exemption.

Federally Required MaineCare Off-Cycle Provider Revalidation Plan: October 2026 Update

Oct 13, 2026

As previously communicated, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) requested all states develop and submit a comprehensive two-year provider revalidation strategy, with priority given to revalidating high-risk providers. 

You can find Maine’s two-year plan and a list of all providers included in the off-cycle revalidation on the Office of MaineCare Services (OMS) Federally Required 2026-2028 Off-Cycle Revalidation Plan webpage. OMS grouped providers into five cohorts and sends notices alerting providers at least 30 days prior to initiating the revalidation window for their assigned cohort. OMS additionally sends a 60-day post-initiation notice, per standard revalidation practices.

Milestones to note:

Cohorts 1 & 2: Individual high-risk providers, providers without an NPI, Personal Care Agencies, Home Health Agencies, Hospice, and Assisted Living Services providers

  • On July 19, 2026, OMS mailed a 30-day notice to impacted providers in Cohorts 1 and 2 announcing that their revalidation window would open on August 17, 2026.
  • Providers in Cohorts 1 and 2 who do not submit a revalidation case by Friday October 16, 2026, will have claims pend until they submit their revalidation case.
  • Providers who miss the October 16th deadline will have until November 16, 2026, to submit their revalidation case. Any provider who has not submitted a required revalidation case by that date will be terminated effective November 17, 2026.

You can find more information about the provider revalidation process on our Provider Enrollment and Revalidation webpage.

Questions?

For questions about this off-cycle revalidation process, please email Kenneth Jamison, Provider Enrollment Manager. For general assistance with the revalidation process, please contact the Provider Services Call Center at 1-866-690-5585, Option 7 for Revalidation Questions, or email MaineCare Enrollment.

The Department remains committed to program integrity, responsible stewardship, and clear communication with providers throughout this process. We will continue to share information with providers through usual communication channels as appropriate.
